title: Book One · Chapter 53: Leo's Card
story:
Leo brings a folded card to school on Monday. It has a red border and his father's handwriting inside.

Leo takes out his reading book. Ronan sees the card beside it. Is it a birthday card for him? Leo puts it away quickly.

“Is that mine?” Ronan asks.

“No.”

“Whose is it?”

“It is about my aunt. Dad wrote it for Mum. I need to give it to her after school.”

Ronan tries to look past Leo's arm. He can see a number at the open edge. Is it a train time? Leo can read train times. Ronan wants to read them, too.

Leo closes the card.

“Don't read it.”

“I only saw a bit.”

“Then stop at a bit.”

Leo's sharp voice upsets Ronan. He moves his book across the desk and doesn't ask any more questions. At break, he speaks to Jun. “Leo has a very secret card,” he says.

“What is the secret?” Jun asks. Ronan almost repeats the number. But the number means nothing to him. Jun may make a guess about it. Ronan cannot give him a real answer.

“I don't know,” he says. “It's for his aunt.”

Jun loses interest. Jun has a paper game for tomorrow. He wants to show it to Ronan. It is a little board with squares and safe corners. Ronan listens to the game rules. Ronan is glad. Now they can talk about the game.

At the end of the day, Leo cannot find the card. He takes everything out of his bag. The stone falls from a side pocket and hits his shoe.

“Under your book,” Ronan says.

It isn't there. Leo looks in the bag again. His hands move quickly. “I lost the card,” he says. His voice shakes.

“Can I help you look?” Ronan asks. Leo nods. Ronan looks on the floor. They find the card between two exercise books in the shared desk space. It is still folded. The red border shows at one edge.

Ronan keeps the card closed. He gives it back.

“I spoke to Jun about your card,” he says. “I called it secret. That was wrong.”

Leo holds it flat between his hands.

“The card has my aunt's visit time. Dad wrote it down for Mum. Now she can check the time.”

“That is your family's news. You can keep it private.”

“I know. I can tell you that part.”

On the way home, Ronan asks about the card. “Why can't I read it?” he asks. “There's nothing bad in it.”

A cart passes them. Mum waits beside Ronan and thinks.

“My sewing notebook has no bad things in it. But it has customer names and payments. I do not want everyone to read those.”

“Their names are private?”

“Yes. And the work is mine. We can choose to share some parts.”

At home, Dad is ready to go back to Mr Sun. He checks the address card in the notebook and closes it. Ronan doesn't reach to see the other pages.

Instead, he puts a small folded birthday invitation on Mrs Lan's chair. He writes her name outside. Inside, he writes a question. WOULD YOU LIKE NOODLES WITH US ON TUESDAY EVENING?

Mrs Lan reads it later and comes to thank him. She can finish her errands first. Then she can join them. “Yes, please,” she says.

“Can I show Mum your answer?” Ronan asks.

“Please do. She's making the noodles.”

He carries the opened note to the kitchen. Mrs Lan read the note first. Then she said, “Show it to Mum, too.” Ronan gives the note to Mum. She reads it and adds one place for dinner.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：share＝分享；folded＝折起的；closes＝合上；invitation＝邀请。

理解问题：

1. Ronan 为什么想看 Leo 的卡片？
2. 他怎样处理已经看到的一小部分内容？
